title: _async_update_data's generic arm logs ERROR with a traceback on every cycle of a persisting failure
claim: A persisting unexpected exception in the update cycle is logged by the integration as ERROR 'Error updating Heat Pump Optimizer' with exc_info on every refresh (3 of 3 refreshes that follow an already-failed update), while the UpdateFailed arm beside it was fixed (#216, D10-09) precisely so a day-long outage would not print the same ERROR every cycle.
mechanism: coordinator.py `_async_update_data`: `except (UpdateFailed, ConfigEntryAuthFailed): raise` (the raiser's latch already logged once) then `except Exception as err: _LOGGER.error(..., exc_info=True); _raise_update_failed(...)` with no latch. Home Assistant's DataUpdateCoordinator already logs the failure on the transition ('Error fetching ... data'), so each later cycle adds one ERROR with a full traceback: at the default 15-minute interval about 96 tracebacks a day for one stuck fault, on Raspberry-Pi-class storage. `_async_first_refresh_light` repeats the arm on every setup retry (coordinator.py:6195).

evidence.unit: integration ERROR records added in refreshes A1, A2, B1 (each follows an already-failed update)
evidence.machine: orchestrator Mac, Apple M1 (darwin arm64, 8 cores), shared box

instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._async_update_data (the `except Exception` handler at coordinator.py:6148; its try body forced to raise by d1s3hook.py), driven through DataUpdateCoordinator.async_refresh on a real asyncio loop

perturbation.change: the generic arm logs ERROR only on the transition: `(_LOGGER.error if self.last_update_success else _LOGGER.debug)(...)` (`--perturb`, in memory at import via excepts_inject.py --edit)

metric_definition: Count of the armed refreshes A1, A2, B1 (each preceded by a failed update) whose added records include the integration's ERROR 'Error updating Heat Pump Optimizer: %s'.
phenomenon_property: A persisting failure is logged above DEBUG once per outage (on the transition), never on every cycle, at every update-wrapper arm.

null_control.note: the disarmed refresh B2 succeeds and adds no such record (only the base class's 'recovered' INFO); the transition ERROR in setup A and setup B is kept under the perturbation

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._async_update_data and _async_first_refresh_light generic arms: log ERROR on the transition (last_update_success) or through log_held, DEBUG after; coordinator.py only.
